projects.name: Solar + Energy Storage on Garage
projects.description: Install 5-7 solar panels on south-facing garage roof face (20x12 ft, ~2-2.8 kW) plus battery storage. Solar = standalone ROI investment (~5yr payback at $0.42/kWh). Battery = generator alternative (no lot space for generator). 30% federal ITC applies to both when paired.
projects.notes: DESIGN: South garage face only. 5 portrait panels = 2.0 kW; 7 mixed = 2.8 kW. ~3,200-4,500 kWh/yr production (20-26% offset). All-in after ITC: solar ~$9-10k, battery ~$9-10k. VENDORS: Sunergy (sunergy.com) — EnergySage 2026 CA Installer of Year, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door. NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com) — Diamond Certified, 35yr, San Mateo County, 40yr warranty. Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy) — online only. AVOID: Sunrun.

tasks.title: Analyze energy usage and size system
tasks.notes: 17,178 kWh/yr at $0.42/kWh avg. Target: 5-7 panels south garage face (20x12 ft) = 2-2.8 kW. ~5yr payback after ITC.

tasks.title: Research and shortlist solar installers
tasks.notes: Shortlist: Sunergy (sunergy.com, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door), NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com, Diamond Certified, San Mateo County), Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy, online only). Avoid Sunrun.

tasks.title: Contact installers for quotes
tasks.notes: Spec: south garage face (20x12 ft, 5-7 panels, ~2-2.8 kW), paired battery (Enphase IQ or Powerwall 3), detached garage sub-panel interconnect. Ask each for: $/W, panel brand, inverter type, battery spec, warranty, timeline, ITC total. Request free shade/LIDAR analysis.

tasks.title: Compare quotes and select installer
tasks.notes: Prefer Enphase microinverters over string inverter. Compare $/W, battery spec, warranty, timeline. 30% ITC on full system incl. battery.

tasks.title: Confirm ITC timing — credit files in year PTO is granted
tasks.notes: 30% federal ITC on Form 5695. Claimed in tax year Permission to Operate granted by PG&E. Battery qualifies only when solar-paired. Plan install timing accordingly.

insights.summary: The gradual decline in device count to 23 combined with zero camera activity aligns with typical late-night device sleep cycles rather than occupants leaving, confirming a quiet, normal Saturday night with no security concerns.

The sustained high device count dropping to 24–25 around 10:27 PM, combined with zero camera activity, confirms all residents are settled indoors and stationary, likely in bedrooms, with the device drop marking the start of the bedtime routine; this resolves earlier correlation flags as normal late-Saturday behavior.

The sustained presence of 28–30 devices with zero camera activity on a Saturday evening strongly indicates either a large unreported gathering or a network anomaly (e.g., ghost connections or IoT malfunction), as this far exceeds the household's expected device count and may impact smart home automation.

The sustained high device count (26–31) combined with rapid fluctuations and zero camera activity strongly suggests a large gathering of guest devices or Wi-Fi presence detection noise rather than actual movement. This cross-signal pattern confirms the readings are likely sensor artifacts, indicating a normal Saturday evening gathering rather than a security or operational issue.

The device count steadily dropped from ~28 to 22 between 15:54 and 16:03, indicating a group departure around 16:00, but the complete lack of camera motion during this exit reveals a coverage blind spot (likely the garage or side yard) that should be addressed.

The sustained presence of 23–28 devices combined with zero camera activity on a Saturday afternoon strongly indicates a quiet gathering or playdate is underway, with guests occupying camera blind spots or remaining still. This is a typical weekend social pattern and requires no action.

The sustained presence count of 24-26 devices combined with zero camera activity indicates the count is driven by personal IoT devices (phones, tablets, smart displays, laptops) rather than human guests, confirming normal Saturday household tech usage rather than a gathering.

The sustained high device count (22-26) over 40 minutes on a Saturday afternoon, combined with zero camera triggers, confirms a planned indoor gathering rather than transient visitors or network anomalies; no action required.

The consistently high presence count (23-27 devices) on a Saturday morning strongly indicates a gathering of guests, which explains the lack of camera motion alerts and confirms normal social activity. The gradual dip to 23 by 10:14 suggests guests are moving to another floor or beginning to depart.

The presence count remaining exactly at 26 devices for over 3.5 hours, combined with zero camera activity, confirms the entire household is still asleep with no early risers or intruders, establishing a normal baseline for the day.
